findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:0 verificationEvidence command field (transition-orchestrator.ts) records grep -n "persistClaim = acquireMkdirLock|store.writeChecklist(args.storyId, reopenChecklist)|store.writeStory(args.storyId, story)|persistClaim.release()" packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts with a bare | for alternation. Default (BRE) grep treats | as a literal character, not alternation, so running the recorded command verbatim produces ZERO output -- not the four matching lines (859/935/937/940) the note claims. Confirmed by running it verbatim in this worktree (no output) vs with -E added (matches all four lines as described). The underlying factual claims in the note are independently verified TRUE (I re-derived the same line numbers, the single REOPEN assignment site at line 651, PHASE_EVENT_BY_TARGET lacking REOPEN, and store.writeJsonFile tmp+rename at store.ts:133-145), so this is not a coverage gap -- it is a reproducibility/hygiene defect in the recorded command string of an otherwise-adequate docs_check evidence entry.

plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts:266,299,302,314 use 4 unnecessary `as any` casts ((e as any).fromPhase/.toPhase, reopenEvents[0] as any) on the new reopen-persistence + normal-transition-shape assertions. ProcessEvent (core/types.ts) already declares `[key: string]: unknown`, so `e.fromPhase` / `e.toPhase` / `reopenEvents[0].transitionType` resolve to `unknown` without any cast, and `unknown` compares/assigns fine against string literals in assert.equal/hasOwnProperty.call under this project's strict tsconfig. Verified empirically: in an isolated scratch git-worktree copy (separate from the shared REVIEW worktree/dist per the concurrency-hazard note) I removed all 4 casts, ran `npm --prefix packages/main run build` (tsc, strict) -> 0 errors, and reran `node packages/main/dist/tasks/plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js` -> both smoke assertions still pass unchanged. So the casts add no compile-time necessity; they just suppress the (already-weak, index-signature-typed) safety net for no benefit. Low severity: test-only file, no behavior difference, `as any` here does not actually widen acceptance beyond what the index signature already allows (a property-name typo would still silently type-check either way) so this is a minor precision/hygiene cleanup rather than a masked-typo risk.
findings.resolvedReason: Removed all 4 unnecessary `as any` casts from plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts (266/299/302/314); ProcessEvent already declares [key: string]: unknown so plain property access type-checks under strict tsconfig. Verified on the real tree: grep -n "as any" returns nothing, build exits 0, plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js and flow-stability-smoke.js both exit 0. Assertions semantically identical.
